source.scope: n>=2, positive closed-ball radius, an actual harmonic neighborhood extension agreeing with the source values, and the normalized unit-sphere law.

items.statement: A function with a harmonic extension near a positive closed ball equals the normalized spherical average of its boundary values at the center.
assumptions: There is an actual function \(v\), harmonic near every point of \(K=\overline B(a,R)\), with \(v=u\) on \(K\). The original \(u\) has no imposed regularity or measurability outside \(K\).

\(\sigma\) is the normalized surface law on \(S^{n-1}=\{\zeta\in\mathbb R^n:\|\zeta\|=1\}\), characterized in the source as the unique Borel probability invariant under every orthogonal transformation. Its literal Lean realization and integrability are justified internally.

assumption_deltas.source: The explicitly real-valued source specialization: n>1, positive closed-ball radius and the source nonopen-set harmonic extension convention.
assumption_deltas.lean: The identical dimension/radius data and one actual total harmonic-neighborhood representative agreeing on the closed ball. Original off-ball u is arbitrary.
assumption_deltas.reason: The total extension representation and literal normalized law require actual source/formal correspondence; no integrability, derivative bound, mean-value or flux result is a theorem premise. The original complex-valued generality is explicitly outside this item.

assumption_deltas.source: Source sigma is the unique all-orthogonal-invariant Borel probability on the unit sphere.
assumption_deltas.lean: Literal Euclidean volume.toSphere normalized by its actual total mass.
assumption_deltas.reason: normalized_sphere_law derives actual probability and exact all-orthogonal sphere invariance through the existing canonical Haar-column identity. Source uniqueness, carrier/integral semantics and this realization are independently reviewed; no unnormalized geometric ds equality is claimed.
